embeds.title: 🔴 Four Vulnerabilities in OpenClaw AI Assistant Can Be Chained to Plant Backdoors
embeds.description:
Cyera reports that four vulnerabilities in the OpenClaw AI assistant (CVE-2026-44113, CVE-2026-44115, CVE-2026-44118, CVE-2026-44112) can be chained together to allow attackers with code execution privileges in the sandbox to bypass sandbox restrictions, escalate privileges, and plant backdoors on the underlying host. Cyera notes there are over 60,000 publicly accessible OpenClaw instances. The vulnerabilities were reported to OpenClaw's maintainers on April 22 and patches were rolled out the next day.
**Sources:** SecurityWeek • 🔴 1 corroborating
**CVEs:** CVE-2026-44113, CVE-2026-44115, CVE-2026-44118, CVE-2026-44112 • **Access:** code execution privileges inside the sandbox via prompt injections, malicious plugins, or compromised external input
**Incident date:** unknown • **Confidence:** claim
[Read source](https://www.securityweek.com/claw-chain-openclaw-flaws-allow-sandbox-escape-backdoor-delivery/)
